newsitem.title: hong kong: Six arrested in Hong Kong karaoke arson case.
newsitem.headline: Six arrested in Hong Kong karaoke arson case.

text.p: Fire inspectors on Sunday sifted through the debris at a Hong Kong karaoke club gutted in a fire which killed 15 people, and police said they were investigating a possible organised crime link to what appeared to be an arson attack.

Initial reports said the fire may have been started by a petrol bomb tossed early on Saturday onto the first-floor stairway of the Top One Karaoke Bar in the Tsim Sha Tsui district of the territory's Kowloon peninsula.
On Sunday, a police spokesman said the case was being treated as arson and murder, but added he was unable to confirm exactly how the fire was started.
"According to the evidence, we have a smell of (paint) thinner," the spokesman told Reuters. "But we cannot say at this time whether it was caused by a bomb or an incendiary liquid."

Police said the Organised Crime and Triad Bureau had drawn up a list of 11 suspects and arrested four men and two women aged between 17 and 28. A search continued for the rest. No details about the detainees were given.
Autopsies would be conducted on the victims' bodies on Monday morning, which should yield more clues, the spokesman said.
The dead included 10 women and five men aged 16 to 42, while most of the injured were young people. Thirteen people were being treated in hospital, with two on the critical list.
About 100 people were in the building when smoke and flames poured up the stairs and through air-conditioning vents into the club. The blaze took firefighters more than one hour to put out.

Local Sunday newspapers carried tragic stories from the fire, including that of two women who died while taking a break from their jobs in a nearby sauna house to join a friend's birthday party at the bar.
The dead were lying in the club's narrow hallways or in small karaoke cubicles, the South China Morning Post reported.
Firefighters said many of the dead were too slow to react because they were intoxicated. "Many did not even notice a fire was going on," one fire officer was quoted as saying.
The bar's management said staff had helped patrons to escape by banging on cubicle doors and warning them of the fire, the newspaper said. Some survivors said there had been no alarm.
Police superintendent Victor Lo told government radio on Saturday that witnesses had said the fire was caused by rival gangs fighting over the protection business in the district.
Police found pipes, knives and meat choppers in the club early on Saturday and another 30 pipes and four choppers in a building stairwell on Saturday night, newspapers reported.

Organised Crime and Triad Bureau detectives arrested a 38-year-old manager of the bar over an assault at the club on Thursday, but he was not a suspect in the blaze as newspapers reported, police said.

Tsim Sha Tsui is a bustling commercial and shopping district crammed with shops, saunas, hotels, restaurants and bars. The area is also known for being a notorious battleground for Hong Kong's most powerful triad societies, the Sun Yee On and the 14K brotherhoods.

"It's a rule that all karaoke bars pay HK$4,000 (US$517) extortion fees to the Sun Yee On triad brotherhood each month," the restaurant manager of a karaoke club near Top One told the South China Morning Post.

Saturday's blaze was Hong Kong's second big deadly fire in as many months. In November, 40 people died in the territory's worst building blaze on record when fire gutted a commercial block in Kowloon's Nathan Road shopping district.
